data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary AUR package that downloads a pinned release from the official upstream GitHub repository. All packaging files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, systemd units, sysusers, tmpfiles, and config) are standard and contain no malicious code, dynamic fetching, or suspicious network activity. The inconclusive verdict from the qwen model was solely due to API errors on three files, not actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by an API failure (HTTP 400) in the qwen model when reviewing three files (komodo-peripheryd.service, komodo-peripheryd.sysusers, periphery.config.toml), resulting in an inconclusive overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified them as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review komodo-peripheryd.service, komodo-peripheryd.sysusers, and periphery.config.toml due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: Implement fallback logic or partial verdicts when a model encounters transient API errors on a subset of files, preventing a single file's failure from marking the entire package as inconclusive if the PKGBUILD and other critical files are verified safe.
Advisory models can serve as a useful secondary check for coverage gaps caused by primary model failures, confirming that the skipped files are indeed benign.
